newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CEN BANK MAKES GOOD ON INTERVENTION PLEDGE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CEN BANK MAKES GOOD ON INTERVENTION PLEDGE.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB), after several months of threatening, intervened on behalf of the Czech crown on Thursday, and said it was prepared to further support the ailing currency if needed.

The crown lost about one full percentage point in early Thursday trading to hit a record low of 5.00 percent against its dollar/mark basket parity, but the CNB, through two waves of intervention, moved to re-invigorate the once steady crown.
"The CNB today intervened on the forex market with the aim of stabilising the crown's exchange rate," a CNB statement said. "If needed, the CNB is ready for further intervention," it added.
At the end of March, the CNB's foreign exchange reserves were almost unchanged from the month before at $11.7 billion.
The CNB did not reveal the amounts it had spent on reviving the crown. The statement added the crown's fall was due to fluctuations of several foreign currencies.
After the moves, the crown steadied at about 3.4 percent on the depreciation side of basket parity. The CNB then fixed the crown 3.4 percent weaker against the basket midpoint.

Tomas Novak, a dealer at bank CSOB, told Reuters the central bank first entered the market at about 0730 GMT on Thursday, but after failing to create a strong change in market sentiment, re-entered to give the crown a further boost.
"At first they were trying with small amounts and now they are continuing with larger amounts," he said during the operation.
The central bank has been threatening to act since February when the crown hit a record high of 5.51 percent on the appreciation side of basket parity.

But Thursday marked the first time it had actually entered the market to move the crown since February 1996 when the band within which the crown is fixed was widened to +/-7.5 percent from a previous +/-0.5 percent.
Analysts said it appeared as though the long-rumoured, but never confirmed, five percent internal band at the central bank -- which if touched would trigger intervention -- had been confirmed.
They added that while the central bank moves would have a short-term effect on the market, further action was needed to stop the crown from weakening again.
"The five percent band appears to be real," said one analyst in Frankfurt.

"(But) I think the market feels that intervention by itself will not be able to sustain the sentiment. Reserves are not that high, so the market overall is still bearish about the currency," he added.
